_what: Which kept rows become journey steps (do-work/keep-steps.mjs). One mapping per kept table and step kind. where is the SQL that picks the rows, written over the table's own columns; each field is a SQL expression over the same row, named in fields: ref (the step's unique key, required), at (when the thing happened; rows are read from the newest kept step of this kind, comparing cutoff_column: the source row's own kept time, an insert time, against the newest journey step's insert time, so a row inserted late with an old event time is still kept), email (made into email_key in JavaScript and never kept raw), visitor (the journey visitor the row carries, when it does), offer_id, value_cents. source maps step source keys to fields. A payment_events row is scoped to the pursuit's own offers: a sale for an offer the pursuit does not sell keeps no step. A client with other table names gives its own mapping in the input, never a code branch.
_cutoff_overlap_minutes_what: A read starts this many minutes before the newest kept step's insert time, so a row whose transaction committed late (after a newer step was kept) is read again. Re-reading is harmless: a step with a ref already kept is left as it is.

mappings.where: event_kind = 'payment.confirmed' AND attributes->>'payment_status' = 'paid' AND attributes->>'offer_id' IN (SELECT id FROM offers)
event_kind = 'payment.confirmed' AND payment_status = 'paid' AND offer_id IN (SELECT offer_id FROM offers)

mappings._what: A lead a site's own form keeps through its action row (serve-a-sites-pages-from-its-rows actions): one statements row, place site-form, meaning lead, its key the action's new id, after holding email, visitor (only with analytics consent), offer_id and self_reported. The same lead step and identity use as a lead the journey kit keeps.

A visit a site's page beacon keeps through its action row (serve-a-sites-pages-from-its-rows actions): one statements row, place site-visit, meaning visit, its key the action's new id, after holding href (the page's address, on the site's own origin), referrer, and visitor (only with analytics consent). The journey kit's own visit step for that address (visitStep: its kept parameters, the touch it followed, joined by touch, else cookie); a direct visit or a check keeps nothing.

A checkout a site's own checkout action started (serve-a-sites-pages-from-its-rows actions, its then step once the payment tool answered): one statements row, place site-checkout, meaning checkout, its key the checkout attempt id, after holding attempt, offer_id, visitor (only with analytics consent) and touch_id (the t of the page the checkout started from). The journey's checkout step, its ref the attempt id, joined by the cookie when the visitor is known, else by the touch.
